newsitem.title: GERMANY: German ABB '96 pre-tax up 24 pct.
newsitem.headline: German ABB '96 pre-tax up 24 pct.

text.p: The German unit of Swiss-Swedish engineering group ABB Asea Brown Boveri AG said on Wednesday that pre-tax profits rose last year, but the gain did not feed through to the company's bottom line.
Pre-tax profits at Deutsche ABB rose 24 percent to 243 million marks ($144.2 million), but net earnings slipped to 121 million from 172 million marks.
Chief executive Michael Pohr, focusing on the pre-tax figure, said the increase was the result of the company's streamlining strategy.
"In many areas our measures to boost competitiveness are taking effect," he told reporters in Heidelberg.

The return on sales rose to 2.8 percent from one percent, and Pohr said he planned to raise that figure to six percent by the year 2000. The company plans to cut its workforce this year by over 2,000 to 27,000.

Sales last year climbed by five percent to 8.7 billion marks at Mannheim-based Deutsche ABB, which is around 97 percent owned by ABB and specialises in transport, electrical and environmental engineering.
Pohr said that despite a sluggish economic environment he expected orders to improve this year, especially from abroad.
Orders in the first quarter of 1997 were expected to rise around 21 percent to 2.4 billion marks, while sales were seen unchanged.
Pohr said he expected pre-tax profits to be stable in 1997, and said equipment investment would total 340 million marks -- up from the 1996 figure of 283 million marks.

The comparison between profits in the latest two years was distorted by extraordinary earnings worth 110 million marks in 1995 which were not repeated in 1996. The 1995 profit figures were adjusted to take account of disposals, the company said.
Group cash flow fell to 498 million marks last year from 658 million.
Earnings per share, based on the formula used by German financial analysts, fell to 27.09 marks last year from 29.16. Deutsche ABB will pay an unchanged dividend of 19.25 marks.
-- Douglas Busvine, Bonn newsroom, 49-228-26097 150 ($ = 1.685 German Marks)
